4. Mr. Rafiqul Haque, the learned Advocate has on the other hand relied upon a number of decisions of this Court where clause (XVI) of Section 10(2) came up for interpretation and reliance has been placed by Mr. Rafiqul Haque, the learned Advocate, on the decision of Commissioner of Income Tax, Chittagong Zone, Chittagong Vs. M/s. Burmah Eastern Ltd, Strand Road Chittagong, (1976)28 D.L.R. 295 and also in the case of Commissioner of Income Tax, Chittagong Zone, Chittagong Vs. Chittagong Ware House Ltd. in the same volume of the D. L. R. at page 98, and in the case of Commissioner of Income Tax, Chittagong Vs. M/s. National Brokers Ltd., Chittagong in 1977 Bangladesh Tax Decisions page 1. In these decisions a view has been taken that for determining whether an expenditure was wholly and exclusively laid out for the purpose of the business, and for commercial expediency, reasonableness of the expenditure has to be adjudged from the point of view of the business man and not of the revenue. It is not disputed that for the officers of the Tea Estates in and around a Club in the name of Balishira Club was set up in the days when the British Companies were in management of the Tea Estates of the area. It is also not disputed that this is the only Club for the officers of the Tea Estates of the area and is run with the contribution of these Tea Estates. 

 5. Forming Club is peculiarly a British concept which was formed by the British planters in the Colonial countries where they frequented and did not have opportunity of having a family life and also for the purpose of maintaining discipline in the administration of the Tea Estates, it was found expedient to have a meeting place of the officers of the Tea Estates where not only they could discuss their common problems regarding business but also could relax and entertain themselves being far "way from the madding crowd. The geographical isolation of these tea estates more or less have remained the same and there are no modern amenities in and around the Tea Estates. The Officers of the Tea Estates live most of their time without their families and the only place where they could relax and entertain themselves in their own class, is this club. Mr. Rafiqul Haque, the learned Advocate has also pointed out that the total income of there Tea Estates which manage this club is Tk. 1,16,13,011/- and the contribution to the Club is only Tk. 8,400/-. It is difficult to accept the argument of Mr. Mozammel Haque, because the learned Advocate has not taken into consideration the other side of the life of the officers who work in these Tea Estates. The fact that the contributions are made by the Tea Estates to maintain the Club shows that these Tea Estates find that the officers frequenting the Club are in a better position to render services to their employer, namely, Tea Estates.
